statement: Which of the following describes all real numbers $x$ that satisfy $-10 < 5 - 3x \le 14$?

choices.misconception: I divided by $-3$ and rewrote the numbers from smallest to largest, but I left the $<$ on the left and the $\le$ on the right where they started.
I subtracted $5$ correctly but then divided every part by $3$ instead of $-3$, getting $-5 < -x \le 3$, and then treated $-x$ as if it were $x$.
I divided by $-3$ without flipping the inequality signs and got $5 < x \le -3$, and since nothing fits that I said there is no solution.

hints: Whatever you do to the middle part you must do to all three parts.
Subtract $5$ from all three parts, then divide all three parts by $-3$. Dividing by a negative number reverses every inequality sign.
Subtracting $5$ gives $-15 < -3x \le 9$. Dividing by $-3$ and flipping both signs gives $5 > x \ge -3$. Now read it from smallest to largest.

solutions.reliable: Subtract $5$ from each part: $-15 < -3x \le 9$. Divide each part by $-3$, which reverses both signs: $5 > x \ge -3$. Written from smallest to largest, this is $-3 \le x < 5$. Check an endpoint: at $x = -3$, $5 - 3x = 14$, which satisfies $\le 14$; at $x = 5$, $5 - 3x = -10$, which fails $-10 < \cdots$, so $5$ is excluded.
solutions.elegant: Each inequality symbol stays attached to its endpoint value. The $\le 14$ part becomes the endpoint $x = -3$ (included) and the strict $-10 <$ part becomes $x = 5$ (excluded), giving $-3 \le x < 5$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
